Specifically, replace the current exclusion condition 'whose net is neither /SENSEC{C}_HI nor /SENSEC{C}_LO' with 'whose net is not /SENSEC{C’}_HI or /SENSEC{C’}_LO for ANY cable index C’ present in the board.' If this protected set is non-empty, also log a warning 'rule58_cross_cable_kelvin_in_corridor_detected' so the manager can observe cross-cable corridor sharing for future keepout geometry decisions. Without cross-cable exclusion, a cable-C ripup treats those segments as 'competitor tracks' and removes them, converting cable C’'s previously-routed Kelvin member to an unconnected ratline and cascading a new Kelvin gate failure onto a cable that was previously clean. Expanding the exclusion to all Kelvin nets prevents this collateral cascade and preserves the integrity of cables that Rule 58 was not targeting.
